pages.title: Scan, Disc, Print
pages.text: The whole loop: $(l)scan$() a build with the Structure Scanner, save it to a $(l)disc$(), then $(l)print$() it anywhere a printer can reach.$(br2)Scans are stored as $(l)blueprints$() in the world save; a $(item)Blueprint Disc$() is the key that references one. Shift+Right Click a written disc to $(l)lock$() it against being overwritten.$(br2)Discs also turn up in $(l)village and exploration loot$() — print what you find, no scanning required.

pages.title: Naming & Tier
pages.text: Every written disc shows its $(l)tier$() — the highest material tier among its blocks (one diamond block in a pile of stone still reads as that tier). That's the lowest machine tier that can print all of it.$(br2)It also shows a $(l)Print Cost$() in that top tier — the total Filament the print needs if you feed it a single top-tier spool (cheaper blocks fold in at the down-conversion rate). Free structural blocks like water and crops cost nothing.$(br2)To $(l)rename$() a disc, drop it in an $(item)Anvil$() and type a name — just $(l)1 level$() of XP.

pages.title: Import & Export
pages.text: Operators can exchange blueprints with other tools:$(br)$(li)$(o)/mc3dprint import <file>$() reads WorldEdit $(l).schem$(), Litematica $(l).litematic$(), and Create / vanilla $(l).nbt$() files from $(o)world/mc3dprint/import/$()$(li)$(o)/mc3dprint export$() writes the disc in your hand to a $(l).schem$()$(br2)Shipped blueprints live in $(o)world/mc3dprint/blueprints/$().
